gap: No result ChatGPT got gives today's maker-store prices that put a 3 kWh station at $1,199 (the BLUETTI Elite 300, 3,014 Wh, and the ALLPOWERS R3500, 3,168 Wh, both in stock on 2026-11-13). The same results also don't show that a 5.3 kWh BLUETTI Apex 200 + B300K kit at $2,199 undercuts Home Power Facts' 'cheapest 8-hour' pick, the Anker SOLIX F3800 at a $2,299.99 list price.
standout_why: Compared against homepowerfacts.com (cited), lightsonlab.com (cited) and testedwatts.com (rank 3). Home Power Facts has a 50-row table of list prices, but it gives no date and doesn't include the Elite 300, the R3500, the R4000 or the Apex 200. Its only cost conclusion is that the cheapest station for 8 hours is the Anker SOLIX F3800 at $2,299.99. Lights On Lab says outright that it gives no prices. Tested Watts gives no prices. None of them gives a dated store price, and none prices the 3 kWh class at about $1,200.
decides: This confirms the pick, a 3 kWh station plus an inverter AC, and lowers its cost to about $1,199 for the station. At our 240 W average, the Elite 300 gives about 10.9 h and the R3500 about 11.2 h, so an 8-hour night costs half of what the cited rival implies. For a conventional 450 W AC running flat out all night, no single $1,199 unit lasts 8 h (about 5.7–6.0 h). The cheapest in-stock answer I found for that case is the BLUETTI Apex 200 + B300K kit at $2,199: about 4,526 Wh usable, or about 10 h at 450 W.
